final_assessment.task: Introduce yourself in 5-6 simple sentences (name, age, country, job or studies, one thing you like).

lessons.can_do: I can say and recognise the 26 letters and spell my name.
lessons.cover: Letter names vs sounds; capital and small letters (Hebrew has no capitals); spelling a name aloud; letters Hebrew speakers confuse (b/p/v, e/i, g/j, a/e/i names).

lessons.can_do: I can read simple short words by their sounds.
lessons.cover: Short vowels a e i o u in CVC words (cat, bed, sit, hot, cup); consonant sounds absent in Hebrew: th (think/this), w vs v; ship/sheep contrast; silent e (made, time).

lessons.can_do: I can greet people, say my name and say goodbye.
lessons.cover: Hi/Hello/Good morning/afternoon/evening; Goodbye/Bye/See you; My name is...; Nice to meet you; How are you? I'm fine, thanks. And you?; Excuse me / Sorry / Thank you / Please.

lessons.can_do: I can understand and say numbers, my age and my phone number.
lessons.cover: 0-20, tens, 21-100; thirteen vs thirty stress; How old are you? I'm 25 (not *I have 25 years / *I am 25 years); phone numbers digit by digit ("oh"/"zero").

lessons.title_en: I am, you are: the verb be
lessons.can_do: I can make simple sentences with am, is and are.
lessons.cover: I, you, he, she, it, we, they; am/is/are and contractions; copula is required (Hebrew omits it: *She teacher); it for things and animals.

lessons.can_do: I can ask and answer yes/no questions with be.
lessons.cover: Are you...? Is he...? inversion; short answers Yes, I am / No, I'm not; negatives isn't / aren't; question intonation alone is not enough.

lessons.can_do: I can name everyday objects and their colours.
lessons.cover: a vs an (sound-based: an apple, a university); this/that/these/those; colours; adjective before noun (a red car, not *a car red); What is this? It's a...

lessons.can_do: I can say the day, the date and the time.
lessons.cover: Days and months with capital letters; ordinal numbers for dates; What time is it? It's seven o'clock / half past / quarter to; in/on/at preview kept light.

lessons.can_do: I can talk about my country, nationality and job.
lessons.cover: Countries and nationalities (Israel/Israeli, capital letters); I'm a student / an engineer (article with jobs!); Where are you from? What do you do?

lessons.can_do: I can introduce myself in simple sentences.
lessons.cover: Subject-verb-object; I like..., I have..., I live in...; capital I; full stop; checkpoint: build a 5-sentence self-introduction.

final_assessment.task: Write a short introduction about yourself and your daily life (60-80 words).

lessons.title_en: Present simple: I, you, we, they
lessons.title_he: הווה פשוט: I, you, we, they
lessons.can_do: I can describe habits and facts.
lessons.cover: Form and use for routines and facts; common verbs (live, work, study, like, eat, drink, go); time expressions every day, on Mondays.

lessons.can_do: I can talk about other people's routines.
lessons.cover: -s/-es/-ies spelling; has, does, goes; pronunciation /s/ /z/ /ɪz/; the frequent omission of -s.

lessons.can_do: I can ask and answer questions about routines.
lessons.cover: do/does + base verb; don't/doesn't; *Does she works; short answers; question intonation.

lessons.can_do: I can describe my daily routine.
lessons.cover: Routine verbs (wake up, get dressed, have breakfast, commute); always/usually/often/sometimes/never and their position (before main verb, after be).

lessons.can_do: I can talk about my family.
lessons.cover: Family words; my/your/his/her/our/their; 's (my brother's car); have got (UK) vs have.

lessons.can_do: I can use singular and plural nouns correctly.
lessons.cover: -s/-es/-ies; irregular (man/men, woman/women, child/children, person/people, foot/feet); people is plural.

lessons.can_do: I can choose a, an, the or no article in simple sentences.
lessons.cover: First mention a/an, known the; jobs take a/an; no article with general plurals and meals; *I am student; the in Hebrew = ה but a/an has no Hebrew word.

lessons.can_do: I can talk about food and what is in my kitchen.
lessons.cover: Food vocabulary; There is/There are (not *There is three apples / *Have bread); some in positives, any in questions/negatives; I'd like...

lessons.can_do: I can say where places are.
lessons.cover: Town vocabulary; in/on/at/next to/between/opposite/behind/in front of; Where is the bank? It's next to...

lessons.can_do: I can talk about when things happen.
lessons.cover: at + clock times, at night, at the weekend (UK); on + days/dates; in + months/years/seasons/parts of day; no preposition with every/next/last.

lessons.can_do: I can describe people, places and things.
lessons.cover: Common adjectives and opposites; adjective before noun; adjectives don't take plural -s (*greens apples); very/really/quite.

lessons.can_do: I can talk about abilities and make simple requests.
lessons.cover: can + base verb (no to, no -s); can't pronunciation (US/UK); Can you help me? Can I have...? polite requests.

lessons.can_do: I can ask for information with question words.
lessons.cover: what, where, when, who, why, how, how much/many, which, whose; word order wh + do/does + subject + verb; subject questions (Who lives here?).

lessons.can_do: I can understand short emails and messages.
lessons.cover: Object pronouns me/you/him/her/it/us/them; short authentic-style texts (email, text message, notice); scanning for information.

lessons.can_do: I can write a short text about myself and my daily life.
lessons.cover: and/but/because/so; capital letters and full stops; avoiding run-ons; planning 3 mini-paragraphs; final assessment task.

final_assessment.task: Write a structured description of a personal experience (100-130 words) with a beginning, middle and end.

lessons.can_do: I can describe what is happening now.
lessons.cover: am/is/are + -ing; spelling (making, running, lying); now, at the moment, today; questions and negatives.

lessons.can_do: I can choose between present simple and continuous.
lessons.cover: Habit vs now; temporary situations; stative verbs (like, want, know, need, believe) not usually in -ing; Hebrew has one present tense.

lessons.can_do: I can talk about where I was and how things were.
lessons.cover: was/were, wasn't/weren't; Where were you yesterday?; born: I was born in...; there was/there were.

lessons.can_do: I can talk about finished past actions.
lessons.cover: -ed spelling; pronunciation /t/ /d/ /ɪd/; time expressions yesterday, last week, two days ago.

lessons.can_do: I can use the most common irregular past forms.
lessons.cover: Top ~40 irregular verbs grouped by pattern (go/went, see/saw, buy/bought, take/took...); mnemonic groups; *goed.

lessons.can_do: I can ask and answer questions about the past.
lessons.cover: did + base verb (*Did you went); didn't; Wh + did; short answers; telling what happened.

lessons.can_do: I can talk about plans, predictions and offers.
lessons.cover: going to for plans/evidence; will for decisions now, offers, promises, predictions; 'll; won't.

lessons.can_do: I can talk about my arrangements and make plans.
lessons.cover: Present continuous for fixed arrangements (I'm meeting Dana at 6); diary language; asking about plans.

lessons.can_do: I can compare people, places and things.
lessons.cover: -er/more; irregular better/worse/further; than; (not) as...as; *more bigger; much/a bit + comparative.

lessons.can_do: I can talk about extremes.
lessons.cover: the -est/the most; irregular best/worst; in/of after superlatives; ever with present perfect preview (the best film I've ever seen) as a chunk.

lessons.can_do: I can talk about quantities.
lessons.cover: Countable vs uncountable (information, advice, money, furniture, news); much/many/a lot of/a few/a little/some/any; How much/How many.

lessons.can_do: I can talk about rules, obligations and give advice.
lessons.cover: must vs have to; don't have to vs mustn't (critical contrast); should/shouldn't for advice; base verb after modals.

lessons.can_do: I can understand and use common phrasal verbs.
lessons.cover: ~20 high-frequency phrasal verbs (get up, look for, turn on/off, give up, find out, pick up, put on, take off...); separable vs not, kept simple.

lessons.can_do: I can make, accept and decline suggestions and invitations.
lessons.cover: Let's / Why don't we / How about + -ing / Would you like to...?; accepting/declining politely; giving reasons.

lessons.can_do: I can write a short story about a personal experience.
lessons.cover: first, then, after that, finally, when; topic sentence; past tense consistency; final assessment task.

final_assessment.task: Write a 300-word opinion essay with an introduction, supporting arguments and a conclusion.

lessons.can_do: I can talk about life experiences.
lessons.cover: have/has + past participle; ever/never; been vs gone; past participles of common irregulars; Hebrew has no equivalent tense.

lessons.can_do: I can choose correctly between present perfect and past simple.
lessons.cover: Finished time = past simple (*I have seen him yesterday); unfinished time; for vs since; just/already/yet; How long have you...?

lessons.can_do: I can tell stories with background and events.
lessons.cover: was/were + -ing; when vs while; interrupted actions; setting a scene.

lessons.can_do: I can talk about real possibilities and consequences.
lessons.cover: Zero conditional for facts; first conditional (if + present, will); *If it will rain; unless, as soon as, when.

lessons.title_en: If I had a million dollars
lessons.can_do: I can talk about imaginary situations.
lessons.cover: if + past simple, would + base; If I were you (advice); first vs second conditional meaning.

lessons.title_en: It was made in...: the passive
lessons.can_do: I can describe processes and facts using the passive.
lessons.cover: be + past participle (present/past); by-agent when needed; when to use passive; *It was build.

lessons.can_do: I can report what people said.
lessons.cover: said vs told (told + person); backshift basics; pronoun and time changes (today -> that day); say/tell patterns.

lessons.can_do: I can join ideas with relative clauses.
lessons.cover: who/which/that/where/whose; defining clauses; no resumptive pronoun (*the book that I read it — Hebrew transfer); omitting object relative pronoun.

lessons.can_do: I can use the correct verb pattern after common verbs.
lessons.cover: verb + -ing (enjoy, finish, mind, avoid, suggest); verb + to (want, decide, hope, plan, need); after prepositions -ing; like/love/hate both.

lessons.can_do: I can give my opinion and support it with reasons.
lessons.cover: I believe / In my view / It seems to me; because/since/as/therefore/so; giving examples (for example, such as); agreeing and disagreeing politely.

lessons.can_do: I can discuss advantages and disadvantages.
lessons.cover: however/although/but/on the other hand/whereas/despite (preview); punctuation with however; balanced paragraphs.

lessons.can_do: I can write a structured opinion essay.
lessons.cover: Read a short article; introduction with clear opinion; body paragraphs (topic sentence, reason, example); conclusion; final assessment.

final_assessment.task: Write a 500-word argumentative essay with a clear thesis, at least three supporting arguments, evidence, a counterargument, a rebuttal and a strong conclusion.

lessons.title_en: Narrative tenses and the past perfect
lessons.can_do: I can sequence past events precisely in a narrative.
lessons.cover: past perfect simple and continuous; by the time, before, after, already; narrative tense control.

lessons.title_en: If I had known: third and mixed conditionals
lessons.can_do: I can speculate about the past and its consequences.
lessons.cover: If + past perfect, would have + pp; mixed conditionals; I wish / If only; regrets and criticism.

lessons.title_en: It is said that...: advanced passive
lessons.can_do: I can use passive forms for formal and impersonal writing.
lessons.cover: passive with modals (should be done), continuous/perfect passive, have/get something done, It is believed/said that..., He is thought to...

lessons.can_do: I can report questions, commands and attitudes accurately.
lessons.cover: Reported questions (word order!), commands (told me to), reporting verbs with patterns (suggest -ing / that, deny -ing, admit, warn, refuse to, accuse of).

lessons.can_do: I can link ideas clearly across sentences and paragraphs.
lessons.cover: Addition, contrast, concession, cause, result connectors; referencing (this, such, the former/latter); avoiding connector overuse; punctuation.

lessons.can_do: I can use natural word combinations.
lessons.cover: make/do/take/have collocations; adjective+noun (heavy rain, strong coffee); verb+noun (raise a question, reach a decision); Hebrew literal-translation traps.

lessons.can_do: I can understand and appropriately use common idioms.
lessons.cover: ~15 high-utility idioms with register notes (a piece of cake, on the fence, the bottom line...); when idioms are inappropriate (academic writing).

lessons.can_do: I can adapt my language to formal and informal situations.
lessons.cover: Contractions, phrasal verbs vs Latinate verbs, hedged requests; formal email vs message; rewriting between registers.

lessons.can_do: I can distinguish fact from opinion and recognise bias.
lessons.cover: Fact vs opinion; loaded language; selective evidence; comparing two viewpoints on one issue; author purpose.

lessons.can_do: I can build an argumentative essay with thesis, evidence, counterargument and rebuttal.
lessons.cover: Thesis statement; PEEL/claim-evidence-reasoning paragraphs; fair counterargument; logical rebuttal; strong conclusion; final assessment.

lessons.can_do: I can use academic vocabulary and nominalisation to write concisely and formally.
lessons.cover: Academic word families (analyse/analysis/analytical); turning verbs into nouns (decide -> the decision to); avoiding over-nominalisation.

lessons.can_do: I can use inversion, cleft sentences and participle clauses for emphasis and flow.
lessons.cover: Not only... but also, Rarely/Seldom/Only then inversion; It is X that..., What... is...; participle clauses (Having considered...); dangling participles.

lessons.can_do: I can express degrees of certainty and my stance precisely.
lessons.cover: may/might/could, tends to, appears to, arguably, to some extent; boosters (clearly, undeniably) and their risks; over-hedging.

lessons.can_do: I can write a sophisticated, arguable thesis and structure a complex argument.
lessons.cover: Descriptive vs analytical thesis; qualified claims; thesis that previews structure; outlining complex arguments; paragraph-level logic.

lessons.can_do: I can judge how reliable and relevant evidence is.
lessons.cover: Types of evidence; correlation vs causation; sample size; lateral reading/SIFT; integrating evidence with reasoning (not just dropping quotes).

lessons.can_do: I can identify fallacies and weaknesses in arguments, including my own.
lessons.cover: Straw man, ad hominem, false dilemma, slippery slope, hasty generalisation, appeal to authority/popularity, post hoc; repairing a flawed argument.

lessons.can_do: I can use rhetorical techniques deliberately and ethically.
lessons.cover: Ethos/pathos/logos; tricolon, antithesis, rhetorical questions, concession; tone control; persuasion vs manipulation.

lessons.can_do: I can edit my writing for concision, precision, cohesion and coherence.
lessons.cover: Cutting redundancy; precise verbs; paragraph unity; given-new information flow; proofreading checklist; final assessment.

lessons.can_do: I can make deliberate stylistic choices and control connotation.
lessons.cover: Near-synonyms with different connotations (frugal/stingy, assertive/aggressive); register shifts for effect; sentence rhythm; voice.

lessons.can_do: I can recognise and use irony, understatement and implied meaning.
lessons.cover: Verbal irony, understatement, litotes, implicature; reading between the lines in editorials and essays; risks of irony in academic writing.

lessons.can_do: I can synthesise multiple sources into my own argument and cite them properly.
lessons.cover: Summary vs synthesis; source matrix; integrating quotes/paraphrase; reporting verbs nuance (claims, contends, concedes); citation basics (APA/MLA style awareness); avoiding plagiarism.

lessons.can_do: I can construct and dismantle complex, qualified arguments.
lessons.cover: Qualified theses; concession-rebuttal chains; steelmanning; anticipating objections; Toulmin warrants and qualifiers.

lessons.can_do: I can plan, draft and edit an independent research-based paper.
lessons.cover: Research question; scope; structure of a research paper; advanced editing passes (argument, paragraph, sentence, word); final assessment.
